messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PAGE: high-rate kv-cache evictions in prod-us-east (p99 latency risk). Pager sent to @oncall. Alert: kv_cache_eviction_rate > 400/min for 5m. Link: https://console.redwood.ai/incidents/1992604832
Sam O'Connor: got it, picking up. seeing a small spike in eviction_rate across a couple of pools. starting triage.
Maya Patel: FYI I already saw a customer support ticket referencing slow completion times in the search pipeline — might be related. Ticket: https://support.redwood.ai/t/5234
Kevin Zhao: quick check — are these the same hosts that had the small kernel OOM last week?
Sam O'Connor: checking host metadata... looks like a different AZ but same instance family (g4dn-ish). not the kernel OOM hosts.
Olga Ivanova: can you paste the last 30s of the eviction metric query? I'll pull kv logs.
Sam O'Connor: query I used: ```rate(kv_cache_evictions_total{region="us-east"}[1m]) * 60``` seeing ~420-650 evictions/min across shards.
Liz Chen: Hmm. That's high but not catastrophic. If it's sustained we risk increased tail latencies. Suggest we silence the noisy alert and create a short-lived alert with an increased threshold while we investigate.
Maya Patel: agree. For customer impact — support ticket indicates 10% error rate on rerank requests. Can someone map which model route that is?
Kevin Zhao: I can. Looks like rerank-prod-v2 route hits the same cache tier.
Sam O'Connor: action plan: 1) Silence the kv-cache alert (5m) 2) Create a metric-annotated dashboard for last 6h 3) Add runbook note and owner 4) Tune alert thresholds and reopen after triage.
Olga Ivanova: I'll take dash + logs correlation. Kevin can help map routes.
Kevin Zhao: on it — making a quick dashboard now.
Oncall Rotation Bot: @Sam O'Connor you are the current pager — reminder to update post-incident runbook.
Sam O'Connor: doing the silence now. `/incident silence kv-cache-eviction --for 5m`
IncidentBot: Silence applied by Sam O'Connor for 5m.
Liz Chen: while it's silenced, create a focused dashboard: panels for eviction rate, cache hit ratio, downstream p95/p99, and rerank error rate. Add a time-range selector defaulted to 6h.
Olga Ivanova: dash done: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/d/kv-eviction-triage?org=redwood
Olga Ivanova: pinned a log query to the dash: `service:kvcache AND eviction_count>0 | json` — helps find keys/clients causing churn.
Maya Patel: I see correlation: sudden increase in a client (internal batch job) that spikes prefixes. Possibly a regression in the batch reindex job.
Kevin Zhao: I can throttle that job if we confirm. Who owns it?
Maya Patel: infra-data owns it but cross-team. I can ping them. @Kevin can you add a temporary rate limit on that route at the routing layer?
Kevin Zhao: yes, adding a 20% ingress cap for rerank-prod-v2 for next 30m. Applying now.
Sam O'Connor: update: ingress cap applied. eviction rate dropped from ~600 -> ~180 within one minute. rerank errors dropping too. good sign.
Liz Chen: cool. Candidate for alert tuning: current threshold 400/min is too low for today's workload patterns. Suggest move to 750/min with a longer window (10m) to avoid transient noise, plus a warning alert at 250/min.
Olga Ivanova: agree on hysteresis. Also add a tag to the alert: `owner:platform-observability` and add runbook link.
Sam O'Connor: I'm updating the runbook now: https://console.redwood.ai/runbooks/kv-cache-eviction?edit=1 
Sam O'Connor: runbook edits: added recent incident summary, link to dash, mitigation steps (throttle job, throttle route), and owner assignment.
Sam O'Connor: also adding an annotation to the alert policy: `last_tuned: 1992604832`, `tuned_by: Sam O'Connor`, `reason: batch job spike causing noisy alerts`
IncidentBot: Note saved to incident timeline.
Maya Patel: I've messaged infra-data to put a backstop on the batch job. Also requested they run a post-mortem with a remediation to avoid reindexing hot prefixes.
Kevin Zhao: PR for alert change opened: https://github.com/redwood/observability/pull/842 — changes: warning @250/min (5m), critical @750/min (10m), owner=platform-observability.
Liz Chen: Nice. Can someone run the alert rule against last 30 days to see how many false positives we'd have with new thresholds?
Olga Ivanova: running adhoc: result — new critical would have fired 3 times (all legit), warning fired 12 times but most were expected due to steady growth. I'll paste table in runbook.
Sam O'Connor: tagging follow-ups in runbook (action items): - infra-data to add rate-limiter on batch job (owner: infra-data) - observability to merge PR and rollout (owner: Liz Chen) - product to review if rerank route can be optimized to reduce cache churn (owner: Maya Patel)
Oncall Rotation Bot: Reminder: please close the page after this thread if mitigations are complete.
Sam O'Connor: mitigations look stable. eviction rate at ~150/min, p99 latency back to baseline. I'll close the page in 10m after monitoring.
Maya Patel: added customer-facing note to the support ticket summarizing impact and mitigation.
IncidentBot: Page closed by Sam O'Connor. Duration: 16m. Incident link: https://console.redwood.ai/incidents/1992604832/postmortem
Sam O'Connor: post-incident: I updated the runbook with an "annotation" section linking the PR and dash, added a short checklist for future oncall (silence -> cap -> patch -> annotate), and set the default alert escalation contact to platform-observability.
Liz Chen: I'll own merging the alert PR and schedule a short monitoring window after rollout.
Olga Ivanova: I'll write a quick kibana saved search and attach to runbook.
Kevin Zhao: noting metric owners in the runbook so next time oncall knows who to ping.
Sam O'Connor: thanks all. main takeaways: noisy alert from legitimate batch spike, resolved by short-term ingress cap + infra throttle. Tune alert to reduce noise, document steps in runbook, assign owners.
Maya Patel: +1, and we'll coordinate a follow-up retro next week to prevent recurrence. :calendar:
